text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'inference-runtime-prod' -> escalation policy 'platform-oncall'. Alert key: pd_abc123. Trigger: 500 responses from inference gateway (spike for region us-east-1). Linked routing: service bound to 'analytics-oncall' (unexpected).
Alice Kim: ACKing. I'm seeing a ~15% 5xx rate on the edge for a subset of inference requests. Some retries causing customer-facing timeouts.
Ben Cho: Wait — it looks like PD sent to analytics-oncall instead of ml-inference team. Did a rotation change go out last night?
Carlos Mendez: I pulled the PD binding — the service id matches inference-runtime-prod but the escalation policy points to analytics. We had a partial rotation update at 02:12 UTC yesterday for night overlap. Might be stale policy id.
Tess Rao: I'm going into PD console now. Running quick check: `pd services show inference-runtime-prod --fields escalation_policy,integrations`
Tess Rao: output (summary): `escalation_policy: ep_42-old -> analytics-escalation-v2` (yep, wrong). Integration: webhook -> routing-syncer.
pagerbot: Escalation note: second-level escalation firing to analytics-sre. Pager count: 2.
Liam Park: I can take primary. Oncall handoff: @Alice Kim hand off to @Liam Park in 2m unless you want to stay.
Alice Kim: hand off to @Liam — I'm shifting to mitigation (scaling + cache fallback). Please own the PD side if it routes weird.
Liam Park: Rerouting incident to correct responders. Running manual reroute: ```
# pd-cli (internal wrapper)
pd incidents reroute pd_abc123 --to-service inference-owners --note "manual reroute: analytics binding was incorrect"
```
Ben Cho: Also adding a suppress rule for analytics team so they don't keep getting duplicate pages: `pd rules create-suppress --target analytics-escalation-v2 --until +30m`
Carlos Mendez: From telemetry: root cause likely a misapplied rotation patch in the schedule-syncer job. The syncer wrote an old escalation_policy id for inference-runtime-prod when it retried.
Alice Kim: Mitigation update: scaled inference fallback pool + enabled readonly cache replica for 95th percentile heavy prompts. Error spike down from 15% -> 2% in the last 6 minutes. Latency stable.
Tess Rao: I've edited the service binding to point to `inference-owners` and verified escalation chain. Also disabled automatic sync for that service until we patch the syncer.
Liam Park: Noting customer impact: telemetry shows 17 orgs experienced increased 5xx; 2 enterprise seats (org-omega, org-sierra) saw timeouts >30s. CS alerted and prepping outbound.
Ben Cho: I posted an interim note on the status page draft: "Partial service degradation for inference API in us-east-1; mitigations applied; investigations ongoing." Will publish once we confirm stable for 10m.
Carlos Mendez: Action items: 1) revert the nightly rotation change (PR #4982), 2) add validation in syncer to prevent stale escalation ids, 3) postmortem owner (Carlos).
Alice Kim: Confirmed fallback sustained. I'll close the PD incident after 15m stable and CS ping.
Tess Rao: Opening a follow-up ticket for PD config hygiene and add an integration test for service->escalation binding. Tagging ops-sre.
Liam Park: Will keep monitoring. If error rate creeps up we'll reopen. For now I'm silencing analytics-escalation-v2 to avoid noise.
incident-bot: Incident pd_abc123 marked as acknowledged by Alice Kim.
incident-bot: Incident pd_abc123 transitioned to resolved by Alice Kim (closing notes: manual reroute to inference-owners; scaled fallback pool; schedule-syncer patch queued).
Alice Kim: Closing thread here — postmortem to follow tomorrow with timeline and alerting changes. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
